analysis.investment_thesis: Angel One is a financial company that must be excluded from the Magic Formula, and even setting that aside, FY2026 reveals the first meaningful earnings cycle turn: revenue fell from INR 5,239 Cr to INR 5,137 Cr and net profit dropped 22% YoY to INR 915 Cr as SEBI's F&O restrictions bit into volumes. The combination of declining earnings, surging borrowings, and mediocre ROE/ROCE of ~15% gives me no reason to own this name.
key_strengths: Scale achieved: 9Y revenue CAGR of 31.4% from INR 440 Cr (2017) to INR 5,137 Cr (2026) reflects genuine market share gains in retail broking
Gross margin of 84.8% reflects the high-margin, technology-driven broking model with operating leverage during bull markets
Strong institutional confidence with FII (12.5%) + DII (18.1%) collectively holding 30.6% of float
key_risks: SEBI's F&O curbs directly threaten the highest-margin revenue line; FY2026 is the first visible proof of earnings fragility
Borrowings surged from INR 788 Cr (2023) to INR 7,951 Cr (2026) — a 10x increase in 3 years — as margin funding book expanded into a cyclical downturn
ROE of 15.6% and ROCE of 14.8% are unexceptional for the capital employed; the business is not earning Magic Formula-quality returns on its assets
red_flags: OCF was -INR 4,142 Cr in FY2026, the worst in the company's history — margin funding book is absorbing capital faster than profits generate it
Net profit declined 22% YoY in FY2026 to INR 915 Cr, breaking a multi-year growth streak — this is likely the beginning of a down-cycle, not a one-off
Financial company structurally excluded from Magic Formula; and even qualitatively, the ROIC trend is deteriorating not improving
analysis.detailed_analysis: As a capital-markets company, Angel One is excluded from Magic Formula ranking because debt and client-margin liabilities distort both EBIT and the capital base. Setting that aside, the qualitative picture has deteriorated sharply: profits down 22% in FY2026, finance costs nearly doubled to INR 437 Cr, and borrowings jumped to INR 7,951 Cr. The discount-broking model proved highly scalable in the 2020–2025 retail-trading boom, but SEBI's intervention in F&O — historically the highest-margin segment — has removed the growth engine. I would need to see earnings yield above 12% and a demonstrated ROIC above 20% to get interested, and neither is remotely achievable at current metrics.
